folds.subject: Disease, drought and salinity resistance and its correlation to mycorrhizae
folds.why: Disease defense and drought and salt stress are distinct effects with enough detail to justify one topic.

folds.subject: Sugar-water/mineral exchange
folds.why: The reciprocal transfer of plant carbon and fungal water and minerals is a central, distinct topic.

folds.subject: Formation
folds.why: Recognition, signaling, and colonization form a distinct account of how the association begins.

folds.subject: Mechanisms
folds.why: Its sentences elaborate how fungal hyphae improve nutrient absorption, already covered by the exchange topic.

folds.subject: Resistance to insects
folds.why: Network warning signals and their effects on aphids and parasitoids are a distinct topic.

folds.subject: Colonization of barren soil
folds.why: Its two sentences describe further growth benefits and consequences of lacking mycorrhizae.

folds.subject: Resistance to toxicity
folds.into: Disease, drought and salinity resistance and its correlation to mycorrhizae
folds.why: This single sentence adds metal toxicity to the same broad topic of plant resistance to environmental stress.

folds.subject: Arbutoid mycorrhiza
folds.why: It has a distinct host group and a defining combination of ectomycorrhizal and intracellular traits.

folds.subject: Monotropoid mycorrhiza
folds.why: Its parasitic, fungus-fed relationship is a distinct mycorrhizal type.

folds.subject: Dual mycorrhiza
folds.why: The ability to associate with two fungal types and its ecological implications form a distinct topic.

folds.subject: Similar symbiotic relationships
folds.why: The sentences define endophytes and distinguish them from mycorrhizal fungi.

folds.subject: Mucoromycotina fine root endophytes
folds.why: The two sentences give a brief taxonomic correction and distinction within the overview of mycorrhizal types.

folds.subject: Orchid mycorrhiza
folds.why: Orchid dependence and the asymmetric relationship with fungi make this a distinct type.

folds.subject: Arbuscular mycorrhizae
folds.why: Its evolutionary history, anatomy, host range, and nutrient exchange make it a major distinct topic.

folds.subject: Ectomycorrhizae
folds.why: Its evolutionary origins, anatomy, and ecological distribution make it a major distinct topic.

folds.subject: Fossil record and genomic analysis
folds.why: The fossil timeline and evidence for early associations form a distinct topic.

folds.subject: Ericoid mycorrhizae
folds.why: Its origins and retained saprotrophic abilities distinguish it from other major types.

folds.subject: Emergence alongside terrestrial plants
folds.why: It covers when mycorrhizae arose and their proposed role in plant terrestrialization.

folds.subject: Origins in plants
folds.why: Plant ancestry and the evolution of different associations through host switching form a distinct account.

folds.subject: Origins in fungi
folds.why: The independent origins of fungal mycorrhizal lifestyles are distinct from the plant-side account.

groups.why: Both state that mycorrhizal associations with plant roots are generally mutualistic.
The second sentence broadens the disease-resistance claim to plant defense above and below ground.
The latter sentences explain the priming effect and restate its stronger defense response.
The second sentence qualifies and supports the claim that mycorrhizae improve plant performance under salt stress.
These describe the improved nutrient absorption benefit and its physical and chemical mechanisms.
The sentences explain that fungal mycelium makes immobilized nutrients, including phosphate, available to plants.
Both distinguish fine root endophytes from arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi by their fungal lineage.
Both state that arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi belong exclusively to Glomeromycota.
